run.summary: 77 patterns cleared the evidence threshold, 21 of them at high confidence, across 5 kinds of behaviour.

findings.title: NJP Station → Siliguri Central loses its evening
findings.claim: Between 17:00 and 21:00, NJP Station → Siliguri Central runs 15% slower per kilometre than it does across the rest of the day.
findings.interpretation: The evening is when this movement stops resembling itself. If staff or signal timing are allocated on a whole-day average, this is the window that average is hiding.
findings.limitation: The evening window is defined as 17:00-21:00 by us, not derived. The comparison is against the same movement's other hours, so it says nothing about how this movement compares to the city.

evidence.test: Mann-Whitney U on pace, evening greater than rest of day
evidence.effect_unit: % slower per km in the evening

findings.title: Most hours of most movements have no publishable baseline
findings.claim: 790 of 1,200 possible movement-hour-daytype bins carry the 30 observations we publish at — 66%.
findings.interpretation: Everywhere else, the honest output is silence. The engine does not estimate into the gaps, because a baseline computed on a dozen journeys is not something anyone should deploy staff against.
findings.limitation: Raising coverage means lowering the floor, and a lower floor means less defensible figures. 30 is a judgement, and it is the reason this number is low.

evidence.test: count of bins clearing the publishing floor

findings.title: Siliguri Central → Salugara empties at the weekend

findings.interpretation: A movement that clears at the weekend is carrying commuting or business travel, and demand-side measures can reach it. One that does not is carrying something that does not observe a weekend.
findings.limitation: One 2019 window covering monsoon into early winter. Festival weeks are inside it and are not separated out, and a public holiday is counted as whatever weekday it fell on.

findings.title: NJP Station → Champasari is quick but undependable
findings.claim: NJP Station → Champasari ranks 2 of 25 for unreliability but 25 of 25 for slowness — a gap of 23 places.
findings.interpretation: Average speed would put this movement in the wrong queue. It moves well most of the time, which is exactly why the bad days are not planned for.
findings.limitation: Ranks are within these 25 movements only, and both measures pool all hours. A gap in rank is not a statistical test.

evidence.test: rank comparison, buffer against median speed

findings.title: Siliguri Central → Siliguri Central is hard to plan around
findings.claim: A journey on Siliguri Central → Siliguri Central needs 30% more time than typical to arrive on time nine trips in ten — 6 points above the city median of 24%.
findings.interpretation: Budgeting the median 8 minutes fails one trip in ten by 5 minutes or more. A movement that is usually fine and occasionally bad is an operations problem, not a capacity one: something intermittent is happening on it.
findings.limitation: Buffer is computed across all hours and both day types pooled. It says the movement is unpredictable, not when. The zone pair is not a road, and this is 2019 data.

evidence.test: percentile spread of pace (P90 vs P50), seconds per km

findings.limitation: An anomaly here means a departure from this movement's own 2019 baseline at this hour. It is not an incident record, and no cause is attached because none is in the data.

evidence.test: binomial test against the city-wide anomaly rate
